title: $57 Million to Collect a Win. The Court Order Was Fake.

lines.say: Fifty-seven million dollars. That's what one law firm's clients wired, prosecutors said, to collect a twenty-three million dollar judgment that did not exist.
lines.show: $57 million. That's what one law firm's clients wired, prosecutors said, to collect a $23 million judgment that did not exist.

lines.say: The firm had secretly settled their lawsuit, in the other side's favor. Then came a false federal court order, purportedly signed by a U.S. District Judge.
Behind it, prosecutors said, was attorney Scott Rothstein. He ran a one point two billion dollar Ponzi scheme built on settlements and loans that never existed. Sentence: fifty years.
lines.show: Behind it, prosecutors said, was attorney Scott Rothstein. He ran a $1.2 billion Ponzi scheme built on settlements and loans that never existed. Sentence: 50 years.

lines.say: Real trials. Real evidence. The verdict.
